title: The present perfect continuous
summary_es: Usamos el presente perfecto continuo para actividades que empezaron en el pasado y siguen ahora, o que acaban de terminar y tienen un resultado visible. Es la forma natural de decir en inglés 'llevo dos horas esperando' o 'hace tres años que estudio inglés'.

rules.body_es: Se forma con have/has + been + verbo en -ing. En preguntas, have/has va antes del sujeto.
table: She has been working here since 2020.
How long have you been studying English?
examples: I've been waiting for twenty minutes.
Has it been raining all day?

rules.h: Duración hasta ahora: for, since, how long
rules.body_es: Para una acción que empezó en el pasado y continúa. En español usamos el presente ('trabajo aquí desde 2019') o 'llevo...'; en inglés NO se usa el presente simple. For + periodo (for two years); since + punto de inicio (since 2019, since Monday).
examples: We've been living in Medellín for three years.
He's been learning French since January.

rules.body_es: Explica una situación presente causada por una actividad que acaba de terminar o se ha repetido recientemente.
examples: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
I'm exhausted because I've been running.

rules.body_es: El continuo destaca la actividad o la duración; el presente perfecto simple destaca el resultado o una cantidad terminada. Los verbos de estado (know, believe, own, like, understand) no van en continuo.
table: I've been writing reports all morning.

mistakes.wrong: I am working here since 2019.
mistakes.right: I have been working here since 2019.
mistakes.why_es: En español decimos 'trabajo aquí desde 2019' en presente, pero en inglés una acción que empezó en el pasado y continúa exige el presente perfecto (continuo).

mistakes.wrong: I have been knowing him for ten years.
mistakes.right: I have known him for ten years.
mistakes.why_es: Know es un verbo de estado y no se usa en forma continua.

mistakes.wrong: She has been working here for 2018.
mistakes.right: She has been working here since 2018.
mistakes.why_es: Since va con un punto de inicio (2018); for va con un periodo (five years).

mistakes.wrong: How long time have you been waiting?
mistakes.right: How long have you been waiting?
mistakes.why_es: Calco de '¿cuánto tiempo...?': en inglés basta con 'How long'.

mistakes.wrong: I've been writing five emails this morning.
mistakes.right: I've written five emails this morning.
mistakes.why_es: Con una cantidad terminada (five emails) se usa el presente perfecto simple.

accept: How long have you lived in Bogotá?

accept: They've been discussing the merger since 9 a.m.
items.explain_es: Punto de inicio (9 a.m.) con since; la actividad continúa.

items.q: I met my business partner in 2010. → I have ...
items.answer: I have known my business partner since 2010.
accept: I've known my business partner since 2010.
items.explain_es: Know es verbo de estado: presente perfecto simple + since.

items.q: I am living in Cali since 2020.
items.answer: I have been living in Cali since 2020.
accept: I've been living in Cali since 2020.
I have lived in Cali since 2020.
I've lived in Cali since 2020.
items.explain_es: Con since y una situación que continúa, no se usa el presente continuo sino el presente perfecto.

items.q: She has been owning that car for ten years.
items.answer: She has owned that car for ten years.
accept: She's owned that car for ten years.
items.explain_es: Own es verbo de estado: no admite la forma continua.

items.q: We have been working here for 2019.
items.answer: We have been working here since 2019.
accept: We've been working here since 2019.
items.explain_es: 2019 es un punto de inicio: since, no for.

items.q: How long time have you been learning French?
items.answer: How long have you been learning French?
items.explain_es: En inglés se dice How long, sin time.

items.q: He has been wrote the report all day.
items.answer: He has been writing the report all day.
accept: He's been writing the report all day.
items.explain_es: Después de been va el verbo en -ing, no el pasado.

items.q: They has been travelling around Asia for a month.
items.answer: They have been travelling around Asia for a month.
accept: They've been travelling around Asia for a month.
They have been traveling around Asia for a month.
They've been traveling around Asia for a month.
items.explain_es: Con they se usa have, no has.

items.answer: I've drunk four coffees today.
accept: I have drunk four coffees today.
I've had four coffees today.
I have had four coffees today.
items.explain_es: Una cantidad terminada (four coffees) pide el presente perfecto simple.

items.q: Have you been wait long?
items.answer: Have you been waiting long?
items.explain_es: Después de been se necesita la forma -ing: waiting.

title: The past perfect
summary_es: El pasado perfecto (had + participio) indica que una acción ocurrió antes de otro momento o acción del pasado. Equivale al pluscuamperfecto español ('había salido') y ayuda a ordenar los hechos en una narración.

rules.body_es: Had + participio pasado para todas las personas. La contracción de had es 'd.
examples: By the time I arrived, they'd finished dinner.

rules.body_es: Usamos el pasado perfecto para la acción que ocurrió primero cuando ya estamos hablando del pasado. Compara: 'When I arrived, the meeting had started' (empezó antes de que yo llegara) con 'When I arrived, the meeting started' (empezó en el momento en que llegué).
examples: When I got to the airport, my flight had already left.
She was nervous because she had never given a speech before.

rules.body_es: By the time, before, after, already, just, never... before, when, because y 'It was the first time...' suelen ir con el pasado perfecto.
examples: By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped.
It was the first time I had seen snow.

rules.body_es: Si las acciones se cuentan en el orden en que ocurrieron, basta con el pasado simple. Tampoco se usa sin otra referencia pasada.
examples: I got up, had breakfast and left for work.
Yesterday I visited my grandmother.

mistakes.wrong: When I arrived, the train already left.
mistakes.right: When I arrived, the train had already left.
mistakes.why_es: Si el tren salió antes de que llegaras, necesitas had + participio.

mistakes.wrong: I had went to the bank before work.
mistakes.right: I had gone to the bank before work.
mistakes.why_es: Después de had va el participio (gone), no el pasado simple (went).

mistakes.wrong: It was the first time I have seen snow.
mistakes.right: It was the first time I had seen snow.
mistakes.why_es: Con 'It was the first time...' en pasado se usa el pasado perfecto.

mistakes.wrong: Yesterday I had visited my grandmother.
mistakes.right: Yesterday I visited my grandmother.
mistakes.why_es: Sin otra acción pasada de referencia, el pasado simple es suficiente.

items.explain_es: El vuelo salió antes de que llegáramos: had already left.

items.explain_es: Salieron antes del momento descrito: had gone out (participio gone).

items.explain_es: Olvidó la tarjeta antes de intentar entrar.

items.answer: had missed
accept: 'd missed
items.explain_es: By the time + pasado simple, y la acción anterior en pasado perfecto.

items.q: Had you ___ (work) in sales before you joined this company?
items.answer: worked
items.explain_es: Después de Had you va el participio: worked.

items.q: The exam was easier than I ___ (expect).
items.answer: had expected
accept: 'd expected
expected

items.q: He apologised because he ___ (not / reply) to my message.
items.answer: hadn't replied
accept: had not replied
items.explain_es: No contestar ocurrió antes de la disculpa.

items.q: It was the first time I ___ (fly) in a plane.
items.answer: had flown
accept: 'd flown
items.explain_es: 'It was the first time' en pasado + pasado perfecto; participio de fly: flown.

items.q: First the guests left. Then I arrived at the party. → When I arrived at the party, the guests ...
items.answer: When I arrived at the party, the guests had left.
accept: When I arrived at the party, the guests had already left.
items.explain_es: Los invitados se fueron antes de mi llegada.

items.q: She finished her degree. Then she started working. → After she had ...
items.answer: After she had finished her degree, she started working.
accept: After she'd finished her degree, she started working.
items.explain_es: After + had + participio para la primera acción.

items.q: The film started at 8. We arrived at 8:20. → When we arrived, the film ...
items.answer: When we arrived, the film had started.
accept: When we arrived, the film had already started.
items.explain_es: La película empezó antes de que llegáramos.

items.q: I lost my keys earlier. Then I couldn't get into the house. → I couldn't get into the house because I ...
items.answer: I couldn't get into the house because I had lost my keys.
accept: I couldn't get into the house because I'd lost my keys.
items.explain_es: La causa ocurrió antes: had lost.

items.q: He sold his car. Then he moved to Spain. → Before he moved to Spain, he ...
items.answer: Before he moved to Spain, he had sold his car.
accept: Before he moved to Spain, he'd sold his car.
Before he moved to Spain, he sold his car.
items.explain_es: Con before el orden ya está claro, así que el pasado simple también es correcto.

items.q: I had never tried sushi before that night. → That night was the first time ...
items.answer: That night was the first time I had tried sushi.
accept: That night was the first time I'd tried sushi.
That night was the first time that I had tried sushi.
That night was the first time that I'd tried sushi.
items.explain_es: 'The first time' en pasado + pasado perfecto.

items.q: The company hired 50 people. Then the crisis started. → By the time the crisis started, the company ...
items.answer: By the time the crisis started, the company had hired 50 people.
accept: By the time the crisis started, the company had already hired 50 people.
items.explain_es: By the time indica que la contratación ya había ocurrido.

items.q: Did she call you before she left? → Had she ...
items.answer: Had she called you before she left?
items.explain_es: Pregunta en pasado perfecto: Had + sujeto + participio.

items.q: When I got to the station, the train already left.
items.answer: When I got to the station, the train had already left.
accept: When I got to the station, the train had left.
items.explain_es: La salida del tren fue anterior a mi llegada: had left.

items.q: I had went to that restaurant before.
items.answer: I had gone to that restaurant before.
accept: I'd gone to that restaurant before.
I had been to that restaurant before.
I'd been to that restaurant before.
items.explain_es: Después de had va el participio: gone o been, no went.

items.q: It was the first time she has travelled abroad.
items.answer: It was the first time she had travelled abroad.
accept: It was the first time she'd travelled abroad.
It was the first time she had traveled abroad.
It was the first time she'd traveled abroad.
items.explain_es: Con 'It was the first time' se usa had, no has.

items.q: They hadn't never seen such a big city.
items.answer: They had never seen such a big city.
accept: They'd never seen such a big city.
They hadn't ever seen such a big city.
items.explain_es: En inglés no se usa doble negación: hadn't + never es incorrecto.

items.q: By the time we arrived, the shop has closed.
items.answer: By the time we arrived, the shop had closed.
accept: By the time we arrived, the shop had already closed.
items.explain_es: En una narración pasada, la acción anterior va con had, no has.

items.q: Had you finish your homework before the class?
items.answer: Had you finished your homework before the class?

items.q: He was tired because he had work all night.
items.answer: He was tired because he had worked all night.
accept: He was tired because he'd worked all night.
He was tired because he had been working all night.
He was tired because he'd been working all night.
items.explain_es: Después de had va el participio (worked).

items.q: After I have finished the report, I went home.
items.answer: After I had finished the report, I went home.
accept: After I'd finished the report, I went home.
After I finished the report, I went home.
items.explain_es: En una historia en pasado no se usa have finished; usa had finished (o finished).

title: The second conditional
summary_es: El segundo condicional describe situaciones imaginarias o poco probables en el presente o el futuro: 'Si tuviera más dinero, viajaría'. Se forma con if + pasado simple y would + verbo.

rules.body_es: If + pasado simple, would + infinitivo sin to. Si la cláusula con if va primero, se pone coma.
table: If I had more time, I would travel.
If she didn't live so far, she wouldn't drive.
What would you do if + past simple?
What would you do if you lost your job?
examples: I would travel more if I had more time.

rules.body_es: Para algo irreal o improbable ahora o en el futuro. Compara con el primer condicional (posibilidad real): 'If I win, I'll...' (es posible) vs. 'If I won, I'd...' (lo veo poco probable). El pasado aquí NO indica tiempo pasado.
examples: If I lived in Cartagena, I would go to the beach every weekend.
If we won the lottery, we'd buy a farm.

rules.body_es: Con el verbo be se puede usar were en todas las personas, sobre todo en 'If I were you' (consejo). En inglés informal también se oye was.
examples: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If she were here, she would know what to do.

rules.body_es: Could (podría) y might (quizás) pueden reemplazar a would en la cláusula principal. Nunca uses would en la cláusula con if.
examples: If you practised more, you could pass the IELTS.
If they offered me the job, I might accept it.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy a house.
mistakes.right: If I had money, I would buy a house.
mistakes.why_es: No se usa would en la cláusula con if; va el pasado simple (calco de 'si tendría').

mistakes.wrong: If I am you, I would accept.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would accept.
mistakes.why_es: Para consejos hipotéticos se usa If I were you.

mistakes.wrong: If I had time, I will help you.
mistakes.right: If I had time, I would help you.
mistakes.why_es: No mezcles el pasado con will; la cláusula principal lleva would.

mistakes.wrong: I would to travel if I could.
mistakes.right: I would travel if I could.
mistakes.why_es: Después de would va el verbo sin to.

items.q: If I ___ more money, I would travel around South America.
items.explain_es: En la cláusula con if del segundo condicional va el pasado simple: had.

items.q: If she lived closer to the office, she ___ by bike.
items.explain_es: La cláusula principal lleva would + verbo.

items.q: If I ___ you, I would talk to your manager.

items.q: What ___ you do if you won the lottery?

If we lived near the beach, we'd swim often.

If the flat wasn't so expensive, I'd rent it.

If there was a gym in my building, I'd exercise.

items.answer: If I had more time, I would learn to cook.

title: The passive voice: present and past
titleEs: La voz pasiva: presente y pasado
summary_es: La voz pasiva pone el foco en la acción o en el objeto, no en quién la realiza. Es muy común en noticias, textos académicos y descripciones de procesos, y suele traducir el 'se' impersonal del español ('se habla español' = Spanish is spoken).

rules.body_es: Be (en el tiempo correspondiente) + participio pasado.
table: The room was being cleaned when I arrived.

rules.body_es: Cuando no sabemos quién hace la acción, no importa o es obvio. Si queremos mencionar al agente, usamos by.
examples: My phone was stolen last night.
Cien años de soledad was written by Gabriel García Márquez.

rules.body_es: Para negar se añade not después de be; para preguntar se invierte be. Las frases con 'se' impersonal en español suelen traducirse con la pasiva y el objeto como sujeto.
examples: The documents weren't signed.
Was the email sent?
Se habla español aquí. → Spanish is spoken here.

mistakes.why_es: El participio de write es written, no wrote.

mistakes.why_es: Falta el verbo be: sin él la frase dice que el paquete entregó algo.

title: Reported speech: statements
summary_es: El estilo indirecto sirve para contar lo que otra persona dijo. Cuando el verbo introductorio está en pasado (said, told), los tiempos verbales suelen 'retroceder' y cambian los pronombres y las expresiones de tiempo y lugar. En estos ejercicios, el estilo indirecto se refiere a algo dicho en el pasado.

rules.body_es: Con said/told, el verbo da un paso atrás en el tiempo.
table: He said he had seen it.
She said she would call. / He said he couldn't come.

rules.body_es: Tell siempre lleva la persona a quien se habla (tell me, tell us). Say no lleva la persona directamente; si se menciona, va con to (said to me). That es opcional.
examples: She told me (that) she was tired.
She said (that) she was tired.

rules.body_es: Cambian según la perspectiva: today → that day; tomorrow → the next day / the following day; yesterday → the day before / the previous day; here → there; this → that; now → then; next week → the following week.
examples: 'I'll see you tomorrow.' → He said he would see me the next day.

rules.body_es: Si el verbo introductorio está en presente (says) o lo dicho sigue siendo verdad, el tiempo puede mantenerse.
examples: He says he's tired.
She said the Earth goes round the Sun.

mistakes.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
mistakes.right: She told me that she was tired.
mistakes.why_es: Say no lleva la persona directamente; con la persona usa tell (o said to me).

mistakes.wrong: He told that he would come.
mistakes.right: He said that he would come.
mistakes.why_es: Tell necesita un objeto (tell me / tell us); sin él, usa said.

mistakes.wrong: Last week he said he will call me.
mistakes.right: Last week he said he would call me.
mistakes.why_es: En el estilo indirecto en pasado, will pasa a would.

mistakes.wrong: They said they have finished.
mistakes.right: They said they had finished.
mistakes.why_es: El presente perfecto retrocede al pasado perfecto.

title: Reported questions and commands
titleEs: Preguntas y órdenes en estilo indirecto
summary_es: Para contar lo que alguien preguntó usamos ask + if/whether o una palabra interrogativa, con el orden de una oración afirmativa. Para órdenes y peticiones usamos tell/ask + persona + (not) to + verbo.

rules.body_es: Ask (+ persona) + if/whether + sujeto + verbo. No se usa do/does/did ni signo de interrogación.
examples: 'Are you ready?' → She asked if I was ready.
'Do you like sushi?' → He asked me whether I liked sushi.

rules.body_es: Ask + palabra interrogativa + sujeto + verbo (orden afirmativo, sin auxiliar do).
examples: 'Where do you live?' → He asked me where I lived.
'What time is it?' → She asked what time it was.

rules.body_es: Tell (orden) o ask (petición) + persona + to + verbo. En negativo: not to + verbo.
table: 'Close the door.' → She told me to close the door.
'Please wait.' → He asked us to wait.
'Don't be late.' → He told us not to be late.

rules.body_es: Los tiempos verbales retroceden igual que en las afirmaciones (is → was, can → could, will → would), y la oración final termina en punto, no en signo de interrogación.

mistakes.wrong: She asked me where did I live.
mistakes.right: She asked me where I lived.
mistakes.why_es: En la pregunta indirecta no hay auxiliar did y el orden es sujeto + verbo.

mistakes.wrong: He asked if was I married.
mistakes.right: He asked if I was married.
mistakes.why_es: Después de if va el orden afirmativo: I was.

mistakes.wrong: My boss told me don't be late.
mistakes.right: My boss told me not to be late.
mistakes.why_es: Las órdenes negativas se reportan con not to + verbo.

mistakes.wrong: She said me to wait.
mistakes.right: She told me to wait.
mistakes.why_es: Con persona + to + verbo se usa tell o ask, no say.

mistakes.wrong: He asked me what time is it.
mistakes.right: He asked me what time it was.
mistakes.why_es: Orden afirmativo y retroceso del tiempo: it was.

items.explain_es: Orden afirmativo en la pregunta indirecta: I was staying.

title: Modals of deduction: must, might, can't
titleEs: Modales de deducción: must, might, can't
summary_es: Usamos must, might/may/could y can't para hacer deducciones sobre el presente según la evidencia que tenemos. Must indica que estamos casi seguros de que algo es verdad; can't, que estamos seguros de que no lo es; might, que es posible.

rules.body_es: Elige el modal según qué tan seguro estás.
table: She might be in a meeting.

rules.body_es: Lo usamos cuando la evidencia nos hace pensar que algo es casi seguro.
examples: He's worked for 12 hours. He must be tired.
The restaurant is always full. The food must be good.

rules.body_es: Para decir que algo es imposible usamos can't. Mustn't expresa prohibición, no deducción.
examples: She can't be at home; I've just seen her at the office.

rules.body_es: Expresan posibilidad. Ojo: para deducción usamos could, no can.
examples: Take an umbrella; it might rain.
He could be in the library.

mistakes.wrong: He mustn't be at home; the lights are off.
mistakes.right: He can't be at home; the lights are off.
mistakes.why_es: Mustn't significa 'está prohibido'; para 'es imposible' se usa can't.

mistakes.wrong: She must to be very tired.
mistakes.right: She must be very tired.
mistakes.why_es: Después de un modal va el verbo sin to.

mistakes.wrong: He can be in a meeting, but I'm not sure.
mistakes.right: He might be in a meeting, but I'm not sure.
mistakes.why_es: Para una posibilidad concreta se usa might/may/could, no can.

mistakes.wrong: They must be work late.
mistakes.right: They must be working late.
mistakes.why_es: Para una acción en progreso: must be + -ing.

items.q: Carlos has been working since 6 a.m. He ___ exhausted.
items.explain_es: La evidencia (trabaja desde las 6) lleva a una conclusión casi segura: must.

items.q: That ___ be Ana's car. She sold her car last month.
items.explain_es: Es imposible: ella vendió su carro. Can't.

items.q: I'm not sure where Luis is. He ___ be in the library, or perhaps at the gym.
The restaurant is always full. The food ___ be very good.

title: Defining and non-defining relative clauses
titleEs: Oraciones de relativo especificativas y explicativas
summary_es: Las oraciones de relativo dan información sobre un sustantivo usando who, which, that, where o whose. Las especificativas (defining) identifican de quién o de qué hablamos y no llevan comas; las explicativas (non-defining) añaden información extra, van entre comas y no admiten that.

rules.body_es: Elige el pronombre según el antecedente.
table: The engineer who designed the bridge is Colombian.
The app which I use most is free.
That's the city where I was born.
The student whose laptop was stolen called the police.

rules.body_es: Información esencial para saber de quién o de qué hablamos. Sin comas. Se puede usar that para personas y cosas.
examples: The woman who called you is my boss.
The report that you sent has a mistake.

rules.body_es: Información adicional sobre algo ya identificado. Van entre comas y nunca usan that.
examples: My brother, who lives in Madrid, is a doctor.
Bogotá, which is the capital, is very high.

rules.h: Omitir el pronombre y no repetir
rules.body_es: En las especificativas se puede omitir el pronombre cuando es objeto del verbo (The book I bought). No se omite cuando es sujeto ni en las explicativas. Nunca repitas el pronombre personal (The man who I met him).
examples: The film (that) we saw was great.
The people who live here are friendly.

mistakes.wrong: The man which lives next door is a pilot.
mistakes.right: The man who lives next door is a pilot.
mistakes.why_es: Para personas se usa who (o that), no which.

mistakes.right: My mother, who is a nurse, works nights.
mistakes.why_es: En las explicativas (con comas) no se usa that.

mistakes.right: This is the book that I told you about.
mistakes.why_es: No se repite el objeto: that ya reemplaza a it.

mistakes.wrong: The girl who her father is a doctor studies with me.
mistakes.right: The girl whose father is a doctor studies with me.
mistakes.why_es: Para posesión se usa whose, no who + his/her.

title: Question tags
summary_es: Las question tags son preguntas cortas al final de una oración, como '¿verdad?' o '¿no?' en español. En inglés se forman con el auxiliar de la oración y el pronombre sujeto, cambiando la polaridad (afirmativa → tag negativa).

rules.body_es: Oración afirmativa → tag negativa; oración negativa → tag afirmativa. Se repite el auxiliar o el modal; si no hay, se usa do/does/did.
table: He lives in Cali, doesn't he?

rules.body_es: I am → aren't I; Let's → shall we; imperativo → will you; There is → isn't there; palabras negativas (never, nobody, hardly) → tag afirmativa; everyone/nobody → they.
examples: I'm late, aren't I?
Let's go, shall we?
Nobody called, did they?
There's a bank near here, isn't there?

rules.body_es: Si la entonación baja, solo pedimos confirmación; si sube, es una pregunta real.
examples: It's a lovely day, isn't it? (baja: confirmación)

title: Too, enough, so and such
summary_es: Too indica exceso (demasiado), enough indica suficiencia (suficiente), y so/such intensifican ('tan', 'tanto'). Cada uno tiene una posición fija en la oración, que es donde suelen equivocarse los hispanohablantes.

rules.body_es: Fíjate en lo que va antes y después de cada palabra.
table: too + adjective / too much + uncountable / too many + plural
It's too hot. / too much traffic / too many cars
She's so kind. / so many people
It's such a good idea. / such nice people

rules.body_es: Too (for someone) + to-infinitive indica que algo no es posible; enough + to-infinitive indica que sí lo es.
examples: The box is too heavy (for me) to carry.
He isn't old enough to vote.
We don't have enough time to finish.

rules.body_es: Expresan una consecuencia. That se puede omitir en un registro informal.
examples: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.

mistakes.why_es: Con sustantivos contables plurales: too many.

mistakes.right: It is too expensive.
mistakes.why_es: Con adjetivos se usa solo too, no too much.

mistakes.wrong: She is such intelligent.
mistakes.right: She is so intelligent.
mistakes.why_es: Con un adjetivo solo (sin sustantivo) se usa so.

title: The third conditional
summary_es: El tercer condicional imagina un pasado diferente al que ocurrió y su resultado, también en el pasado: 'Si hubiera sabido, te habría ayudado'. Sirve para expresar arrepentimientos, críticas y especulaciones sobre el pasado.

rules.body_es: If + past perfect, would have + participio.
table: If + had + participle, would have + participle
If I had known, I would have helped.
If + hadn't + participle, wouldn't have + participle
If she hadn't missed the bus, she wouldn't have been late.
What would you have done if + past perfect?
What would you have done if you had lost the job?

rules.body_es: Hablamos de algo que NO ocurrió (o sí ocurrió) en el pasado y de su consecuencia imaginaria. Es irreal: ya no se puede cambiar.
examples: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight. (Salimos tarde y perdimos el vuelo.)

rules.body_es: Could have = habría podido; might have = quizás habría.
examples: If you had asked, I could have helped you.
If it hadn't rained, more people might have come.

rules.body_es: 'd puede ser had (en la cláusula con if) o would (en la principal). En la cláusula con if nunca va would.
examples: If I'd known, I'd have called. (= If I had known, I would have called.)

mistakes.wrong: If I would have known, I would have come.
mistakes.right: If I had known, I would have come.
mistakes.why_es: En la cláusula con if va el past perfect, no would have (calco de 'si habría sabido').

mistakes.wrong: If I had studied, I would passed.
mistakes.right: If I had studied, I would have passed.
mistakes.why_es: Falta have: would have + participio.

mistakes.wrong: If she had came earlier, she would have met him.
mistakes.right: If she had come earlier, she would have met him.
mistakes.why_es: Después de had va el participio (come), no el pasado (came).

mistakes.right: If I had known about the strike yesterday, I would have taken a taxi.
mistakes.why_es: Para una condición en el pasado se necesita el past perfect.

summary_es: A nivel B2 la pasiva se usa en todos los tiempos y con modales, y también en estructuras impersonales como 'It is said that...' o 'He is believed to...'. Estas formas son típicas de las noticias y de la escritura académica (por ejemplo, IELTS Writing Task 1).

rules.body_es: Siempre be (en el tiempo adecuado) + participio.

rules.h: Pasiva impersonal: It is said that...

title: Future continuous and future perfect
summary_es: El futuro continuo (will be + -ing) describe una acción en progreso en un momento del futuro. El futuro perfecto (will have + participio) indica que algo estará terminado antes de un momento futuro. Ambos son útiles para hablar de planes, plazos y metas.

rules.body_es: Compara las tres formas.

By 2030, I will have finished my PhD.

rules.body_es: Acción en progreso en un momento futuro (at 8 p.m. tomorrow, this time next week). También para preguntar de forma cortés por planes.

rules.body_es: Acción terminada antes de un momento futuro. Muy frecuente con by (para, antes de) y by the time.
examples: By Friday, we'll have sent all the invitations.

rules.body_es: Después de by the time, when, before, etc. se usa el presente simple, no will.

title: Modals of deduction in the past
titleEs: Modales de deducción en el pasado
summary_es: Para hacer deducciones sobre el pasado usamos modal + have + participio: must have (seguro que sí), might/may/could have (posiblemente) y can't/couldn't have (seguro que no). Son muy útiles para especular sobre lo que ocurrió.

rules.body_es: Modal + have + participio pasado.
Conclusión lógica basada en la evidencia.
examples: The ground is wet. It must have rained.
You must have been nervous before the interview.

rules.body_es: Para decir que algo fue imposible. Mustn't have no se usa para deducción.
examples: She can't have been at the party; she was in Lima.

title: Participle clauses
summary_es: Las cláusulas de participio permiten acortar oraciones usando -ing, el participio pasado o having + participio, en lugar de una oración completa con conjunción. Dan un estilo más fluido y formal, ideal para la escritura (IELTS Writing).

rules.body_es: Elige la forma según el significado.
table: Walking to work, I saw an accident.
Built in 1600, the church is the oldest in the city.
Having finished the report, he went home.

rules.body_es: Para acciones simultáneas o para expresar causa, con sentido activo.
examples: Feeling tired, she went to bed early. (= Because she felt tired...)
Not knowing the way, we used the GPS.

rules.body_es: El participio pasado tiene sentido pasivo; having + participio indica que una acción terminó antes que la otra.
examples: Shocked by the news, the minister cancelled his speech.

rules.h: Mismo sujeto y cláusulas de relativo reducidas

title: Articles: advanced uses
summary_es: El uso de a/an, the o ningún artículo es una de las mayores dificultades para hispanohablantes, porque en español usamos el artículo para generalizar ('la vida es difícil') y en inglés no ('Life is difficult'). Este taller repasa las reglas más útiles para B2 e IELTS.

rules.body_es: Los sustantivos incontables y los plurales en sentido general no llevan artículo. Si son específicos, llevan the.
examples: Money doesn't bring happiness.
Dogs are loyal animals.
The money I lent you was for rent. (específico)

rules.body_es: Cosas únicas, superlativos, ríos, océanos, cordilleras, países con plural o 'Republic/Kingdom/States', grupos sociales (the + adjetivo) y the + sustantivo singular para una especie o invento.
table: the Amazon, the Andes, the Pacific
The Andes run through seven countries.
the rich, the elderly, the unemployed

rules.body_es: La mayoría de países, ciudades, lagos y montañas individuales; comidas (have lunch); idiomas y deportes; by + transporte; instituciones con su propósito (go to school/work/bed/university).
examples: Lake Titicaca is between Peru and Bolivia.

title: Linking contrast: although, despite, however, whereas
summary_es: Los conectores de contraste unen ideas opuestas, pero cada uno tiene una gramática diferente: although va con una oración, despite con un sustantivo o -ing, however une dos oraciones y whereas compara dos hechos. Usarlos bien es clave en IELTS Writing (coherencia y cohesión).

rules.body_es: Fíjate en lo que va después de cada uno.
table: Although she was tired, she finished the report.
Despite feeling tired, she finished the report.
She was tired. However, she finished the report.
I like tea, whereas my wife prefers coffee.

rules.body_es: Nunca van seguidos de sujeto + verbo. Si quieres una oración, usa despite the fact that. Ojo: despite no lleva of.
examples: Despite the rain, we went out.
In spite of being tired, he kept working.
Despite the fact that it was raining, we went out.

rules.body_es: However conecta dos oraciones independientes. Va después de punto o punto y coma, seguido de coma. También puede ir en medio con comas.

The plan was good; however, it was too expensive.
Sales, however, have fallen.

rules.body_es: Contrastan dos hechos de forma paralela (A es así, B es de otra forma).
examples: Bogotá is cold, whereas Cartagena is hot.

title: Inversion for emphasis
summary_es: En inglés formal, cuando una expresión negativa o restrictiva (never, not only, hardly, only when...) va al inicio de la oración, el auxiliar se coloca antes del sujeto, como en una pregunta. Da énfasis y un registro elevado, muy valorado en IELTS Writing y Speaking de nivel alto.

rules.body_es: Expresión negativa/restrictiva + auxiliar + sujeto + verbo. Si no hay auxiliar, se usa do/does/did.
table: Never have I seen such chaos.
Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
No sooner had we left than it started to rain.
Only when / Not until / Only after
Only when I read the contract did I understand.

rules.body_es: Hardly y scarcely van con when; no sooner va con than. Normalmente con past perfect para la primera acción.
examples: Scarcely had the meeting begun when the power went out.
No sooner had the CEO resigned than the shares fell.

rules.body_es: Con only when/after/then y not until, la inversión aparece en la cláusula principal, no en la subordinada. Little + inversión expresa que alguien no era consciente de algo.
examples: Not until I spoke to the engineer did I understand the problem.
Little did they know that the company was about to collapse.

rules.body_es: Under no circumstances, On no account, In no way + inversión.
examples: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
On no account must the door be left open.

title: Cleft sentences
summary_es: Las cleft sentences dividen una oración en dos partes para destacar un elemento: 'It was María who found the error' o 'What I need is a holiday'. Equivalen a 'Fue María quien...' o 'Lo que necesito es...' y son útiles para enfatizar, contrastar o corregir información.

rules.body_es: It + be + elemento enfatizado + that/who + resto de la oración. Se puede enfatizar el sujeto, el objeto, el lugar o el momento.
table: It was Laura who designed the logo.
It's the price that worries me.
It was in 2015 that the law changed.

rules.body_es: What + oración + be + elemento enfatizado. Para enfatizar una acción se usa What + sujeto + did + was + (to) verbo.
examples: What I need is a long holiday.
What she did was resign.
What caused the problem was the lack of communication.

rules.body_es: All (that)... is, The thing that... is, The reason (why)... is that, The person who..., The place where...
examples: All I want is a quiet weekend.
The reason why I left was that the company had no future.

rules.body_es: Con What + oración, el verbo be suele ir en singular. Las it-clefts sirven para corregir: It wasn't John who called; it was Peter.
examples: What surprised me was the price.
It's not the salary that matters; it's the environment.

title: Advanced conditionals
summary_es: En inglés formal, los condicionales se pueden expresar sin if mediante la inversión (Should you..., Were it not for..., Had I known...) o con conectores como provided that, as long as, unless y but for. Son típicos de correos formales, contratos y textos académicos.

rules.body_es: Se elimina if y se invierte el auxiliar. Las formas negativas no se contraen.
table: Should you need help, call us.
Were the bank to raise rates, borrowing would fall.
Had I known, I would have stayed.
Had she not warned us, we would have lost everything.

rules.h: Were it not for / Had it not been for / But for
rules.body_es: Significan 'si no fuera por' / 'si no hubiera sido por' + sustantivo. Were it not for se refiere al presente; had it not been for, al pasado; but for sirve para ambos.
examples: Were it not for tourism, the town would be empty.
Had it not been for the GPS, we would have got lost.
But for your advice, I would have made a mistake.

rules.body_es: Provided (that) / providing / as long as / on condition that = solo si (con presente, no will). Unless = if not. Otherwise = si no. Suppose / supposing = imagina que.
examples: You can borrow my car provided you return it by Sunday.
We won't sign unless they lower the price.
Take an umbrella; otherwise you'll get wet.

mistakes.right: Should you need help, call me.
mistakes.why_es: Después de should va el verbo base.

mistakes.why_es: En la inversión no se contrae la negación.

title: The subjunctive and formal structures
summary_es: El subjuntivo en inglés usa la forma base del verbo (sin -s ni tiempo) después de verbos y adjetivos que expresan exigencia o importancia: 'It is essential that he be informed'. Es propio del registro formal (cartas, informes, normativas). Este taller incluye también estructuras como 'It's time we left' o 'I'd rather you didn't'.

rules.body_es: Recommend, suggest, insist, demand, propose, request, require, order + that + sujeto + verbo base (sin -s, sin to, sin tiempo). En inglés británico también se usa should + verbo.
table: The board recommended that he resign.
She insisted that he not drive.
They demanded that the report be published.
They suggested that we should wait.

rules.body_es: Essential, vital, crucial, imperative, important, necessary + that + sujeto + verbo base.
examples: It is essential that every candidate bring a valid ID.
It is vital that the data be kept confidential.

rules.body_es: It's (high/about) time + sujeto + past simple. Would rather + otro sujeto + past simple (aunque se refiere al presente).
examples: It's high time the government took action.
I'd rather you didn't smoke here.

rules.body_es: Algunas expresiones conservan el subjuntivo: Be that as it may (aun así), Come what may (pase lo que pase), If need be (si es necesario), So be it.
examples: Be that as it may, the deadline stands.
Come what may, we will finish the project.

title: Ellipsis and substitution
summary_es: Para no repetir palabras, el inglés sustituye (one, do, so, that) u omite (elipsis) partes de la oración. Dominar estas formas hace que tu inglés suene natural y cohesionado, algo que se evalúa en IELTS Speaking y Writing.

rules.body_es: One/ones reemplaza a un sustantivo contable ya mencionado. That/those reemplaza a un sustantivo en comparaciones formales.
examples: I prefer the blue one.
The salaries in Bogotá are higher than those in Cali.
The population of Lima is larger than that of Bogotá.

rules.body_es: Do/does/did (so) reemplaza un verbo. So/not reemplaza una oración después de think, hope, expect, suppose, believe, be afraid.
table: Is it open? — I think so.
I hope not / I'm afraid not / I don't think so

He promised to call, and he did (so).

rules.h: Elipsis después de auxiliares y to
rules.body_es: Se omite el verbo principal y se deja solo el auxiliar, el modal o to.
examples: She can swim and I can too.
I haven't finished, but Ana has.
I didn't want to go, but I had to.

rules.body_es: Para estar de acuerdo: So do I (afirmativo), Neither/Nor do I (negativo). Me too no sirve después de una oración negativa.
examples: I love jazz. — So do I.
I don't like horror films. — Neither do I.

title: Nominalisation for academic writing
summary_es: La nominalización convierte verbos y adjetivos en sustantivos ('prices increased' → 'an increase in prices'). Produce un estilo más formal, impersonal y conciso, típico de informes y de IELTS Writing Task 1 y 2.

rules.body_es: En lugar de una oración con sujeto + verbo, usamos un sustantivo que resume la acción. Así podemos hablar de procesos e ideas sin mencionar quién hace qué.
examples: Prices increased rapidly. → There was a rapid increase in prices.
The government decided... → The government's decision...

rules.body_es: Muchos sustantivos se forman con estos sufijos.
table: approve → approval, fail → failure, grow → growth, analyse → analysis

rules.body_es: Al nominalizar: el adverbio pasa a adjetivo (rapidly → rapid); el sujeto pasa a 's o of (the company's expansion / the expansion of the company); because + oración pasa a due to / owing to + sustantivo.
examples: Because the train was delayed... → Due to the delay of the train...

title: Hedging and cautious language
summary_es: En la escritura académica se evitan las afirmaciones absolutas. El hedging usa modales, verbos como seem o tend, y expresiones como 'it is likely that' para presentar ideas con precisión y cautela. Es clave en IELTS Writing Task 2 para lograr un tono académico.

rules.body_es: Las afirmaciones absolutas (always, all, prove) suelen ser falsas o difíciles de justificar. El hedging muestra precisión y pensamiento crítico.
examples: All young people are addicted to their phones. → Many young people appear to spend too much time on their phones.

rules.body_es: Combina distintos recursos.
table: This may lead to higher costs.
The data suggest that... / Older workers tend to...
It could be argued that..., There is some evidence that...
to some extent, in some cases, generally
To some extent, the reform worked.

rules.body_es: Likely es adjetivo: be likely to + verbo o It is likely that + oración. Probable no se usa con to-infinitive.
examples: The economy is likely to grow.
It is likely that the economy will grow.

rules.body_es: Demasiadas palabras prudentes juntas confunden. Una sola suele bastar.
examples: Maybe it could possibly be... → It could be...

title: The future in the past
summary_es: El futuro en el pasado expresa lo que en un momento pasado se veía como futuro: planes (was going to), acciones inminentes (was about to), predicciones (would) y destinos (was to). Es fundamental para narrar historias y explicar planes que cambiaron.

rules.body_es: Cada forma corresponde a una forma de futuro, vista desde el pasado.
table: I was going to call you, but I forgot.
I was about to leave when the phone rang.
We were meeting the clients at 5.

rules.body_es: Was going to y was to have + participio son frecuentes para planes frustrados.
examples: We were going to buy a house, but prices went up.
The concert was to have taken place on Saturday.

rules.body_es: Was on the point of / on the verge of + -ing expresan lo mismo de forma más enfática.
examples: She was on the point of resigning when they promoted her.

rules.body_es: Would aparece en narraciones (Little did they know that they would...) y en el estilo indirecto (He said he would...).
examples: In 1990 nobody imagined that the internet would change everything.

mistakes.why_es: Desde el pasado, will se convierte en would.

mistakes.why_es: La estructura es about to + verbo base.

mistakes.wrong: She was to becoming famous.
mistakes.right: She was to become famous.
mistakes.why_es: Was to + verbo base.
